newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, July higher on China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, July higher on China.

text.p: Reports of Chinese demand for U.S. soymeal boosted nearby soymeal contracts to higher closes, while soyoil ended lower, traders said.
Near-limit losses in July soymeal on Monday garnered the attention of soymeal buyers in both China and Europe, traders said.
Beijing traders said China bought up to 200,000 tonnes of soymeal this week from U.S. as well as South American sources.
The trades occurred overnight Monday and Tuesday, and shipment is set for July, August and September, traders said.
Traders in Europe also reported heavy trading in those markets on Tuesday. Shippers were the sellers while feed compounders were the main purchasers, traders there said.
Late selling from soybean crushers in soyoil futures tripped sell-stop orders and caused futures to fall sharply near the close, traders said.
Soyoil futures were also pressured by reports that the Indian monsoon had finally reached southern India after a one-week delay, traders said.
July soymeal settled $1.90 higher at $266.70 per ton and other months were down $2.30 to $4.00 a ton. July soyoil closed down 0.28 cent a lb at 22.95 cents.
